subject: nail biting
title: What If You Bit Your Nails Every Day?

scenes.text: What if you bit your nails every day? Up to three in ten people already do.
The gap under a fingernail is the germiest spot on your hand, averaging about two hundred forty-five thousand bacterial units.
Bite daily and those germs move in. A 2007 study found gut-type bacteria in seventy-six percent of nail biters' mouths.
Among non-biters, it was about twenty-six percent. A 2017 study of two hundred people found a similar gap.
After years, the constant chewing can chip teeth and damage the nail's root, leaving grooves and even scars.
And most biters start around age three or four. Many adults have been snacking on their hands' dirtiest spot for decades.

description:
What if you bit your nails every day? Up to 30% of people bite their nails, usually starting around age 3 or 4 (UCLA Health). A 1988 Journal of Clinical Microbiology study found the space under fingernails averaged about 10^5.39 (roughly 245,000) colony-forming units, far more than other hand sites.
A 2007 study found Enterobacteriaceae in 76% of nail biters' mouths versus 26.5% of non-biters, and a 2017 study of 200 people found 58% versus 16%; long-term biting can damage teeth and the nail matrix, causing grooves and scarring.
